summary: The seed workstation resolved a rare domain shortly before the suspicious TLS session.
Seed JA4 alert matched a suspicious TLS beacon to rare external infrastructure.
The seed workstation reconnected to the same C2 infrastructure after the alert.
Suspicious rundll32.exe launched a loader DLL from a user-writable path shortly after the beacon sequence.
PsExec remote service creation from ws-eng-02 to ws-eng-05 followed the seed beacon traffic.
Approved SCCM patch staging began on ws-eng-05 in the same hour and could explain some routine admin activity.
Windows update content was downloaded from an approved Microsoft endpoint during the maintenance window.
A second workstation contacted the original beacon infrastructure minutes after the remote-service event.
The second workstation resolved a secondary rare domain that did not appear in the seed alert.
The second workstation pivoted to a second external IP over TLS after reaching the original beacon host.
WMI remote process creation from ws-eng-05 to ws-eng-09 followed the secondary outbound TLS traffic.
A third workstation later resolved the secondary domain that emerged only after expansion.
A third workstation contacted the secondary infrastructure after the WMI activity, indicating likely onward spread.
The EDR sensor on ws-eng-09 reported degraded process telemetry, so the execution lineage behind the second beacon cannot be reconstructed.
A QA telemetry job also touched the same hosting IP through a different vendor domain, indicating the secondary IP is shared infrastructure.
